questions.prompt: What is the slope \(m\) of the line passing through \((-3, 4)\) and \((5, -2)\)?

choices.feedback: Upside-down formula! Slope is \(\dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\) (change in \(y\) on top), not \(\dfrac{x_2 - x_1}{y_2 - y_1}\): \(m = \dfrac{-2 - 4}{5 - (-3)} = \dfrac{-6}{8} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\).
Double-negative trap in the denominator! \(5 - (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8\) (not \(5 - 3 = 2\)), so \(m = \dfrac{-6}{8} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\).
Keep the points in the SAME order top and bottom! Using \((-2 - 4)\) on top requires \((5 - (-3))\) on bottom (not \(-3 - 5\)), giving \(\dfrac{-6}{8} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\).

choices.feedback: Great slope \(m = 4\)! To solve \(5 = 8 + b\), subtract \(8\) from both sides instead of adding: \(b = 5 - 8 = -3\).
Watch the sign of \(b\)! From \(5 = 8 + b\), subtracting \(8\) gives \(b = 5 - 8 = -3\), not \(+3\). Quick check: \(4(2) + 3 = 11 \neq 5\).
Swapped \(x\) and \(y\) when solving for \(b\)! With \((2, 5)\), substitute \(x = 2\) and \(y = 5\): \(5 = 4(2) + b \implies b = -3\).

Watch the sign of \(b\)! From \(5 = 3 + b\), subtracting \(3\) gives \(b = +2\), not \(-2\). Checking \((3, -7)\): \(-3(3) + 2 = -7\).

questions.prompt: A line crosses the axes at \((4, 0)\) and \((0, -6)\). What is the equation of the line in slope-intercept form?

choices.feedback: Check the slope sign! \(m = \dfrac{-6 - 0}{0 - 4} = \dfrac{-6}{-4} = +\dfrac{3}{2}\) — a negative divided by a negative is POSITIVE!
Intercept trap! \((4, 0)\) is the \(x\)-intercept, NOT the \(y\)-intercept. The \(y\)-intercept is where \(x = 0\), which is \((0, -6)\), so \(b = -6\).
Flipped rise and run! \(m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \dfrac{-6 - 0}{0 - 4} = \dfrac{-6}{-4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\), not \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).
The slope is \(m = \dfrac{-6 - 0}{0 - 4} = \dfrac{-6}{-4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\), and \((0, -6)\) gives the \(y\)-intercept \(b = -6\) directly. Check \((4, 0)\): \(\dfrac{3}{2}(4) - 6 = 0\).

Watch the axes! The line crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((2, 0)\), but the \(y\)-intercept is where it crosses the \(y\)-axis: \((0, 1)\), so \(b = 1\), not \(2\).
